v3.timing_note: Measured batch prediction time divided among active tasks, not single-request latency.
v3.selection: First initially unfinished cases with an exact five-step solution, selected independently of policy outcomes.

v1.timing_note: Measured batch prediction time divided among active tasks, not single-request latency.
v1.selection: First initially unfinished cases with an exact five-step solution, selected independently of policy outcomes.

paired_success_action_cost.selection: Same legacy scenario IDs completed by both policies. Declared weighted action costs only; neural decision time reported separately.

v3.timing_note: Measured batch prediction time divided among active tasks, not single-request latency.
v3.selection: First initially unfinished cases with an exact five-step solution, selected independently of policy outcomes.

v1.timing_note: Measured batch prediction time divided among active tasks, not single-request latency.
v1.selection: First initially unfinished cases with an exact five-step solution, selected independently of policy outcomes.

goal_changes.selection: Model-independent: both goals unfinished, reachable, with disjoint optimal next-action sets. Same graph, state, and costs per pair.

paired_efficiency.selection: Exactly the same problem and stochastic episode, successful under both methods. Failed episodes cannot make costs appear lower.

belief.cost_note: Tokens and action latency are declared estimates for belief tasks. Decision latency is measured. Weighted cost = tokens + .01*(declared action ms + measured decision ms). No real tool time is claimed for belief simulation.

actual_tools.scope: Real files and subprocess checks on controlled generated interval/collection fixtures, using supplied patches. No code generation or arbitrary repository work.
actual_tools.cost_note: Wall time, tool execution and policy decision times measured; token costs remain declared estimates.

promotion.default_policy_action: Retain prior default policies; do not silently route old tasks to v3

gates.validation_retention: Frozen candidate must already pass the trainer's predeclared strict validation-retention checks
gates.legacy_retention: Matched fresh legacy goal completion >= frozen v1
gates.curriculum_retention: Matched fresh v2-composition goal completion >= frozen v1
gates.legacy_action_cost_retention: Mean declared weighted action cost <= frozen v1 on exactly the same legacy tasks both policies complete
gates.changed_goal_action_retention: Fresh paired changed-goal next-action accuracy >= frozen v2.1
gates.changed_goal_pair_retention: Fresh changed-goal pairs with both members correct >= frozen v2.1
gates.actual_tool_retention: Matched real fixture verified-and-stopped completion >= frozen v2.1
gates.uncertainty_expected: Exact expected verified completion >= each of two cheap baselines
gates.uncertainty_sampled: Matched sampled verified completion >= each of two cheap baselines
gates.useful_efficiency: Strictly lower mean weighted declared action cost plus measured decision overhead on the same episodes both methods complete, against the strongest cheap baseline

protocol.strong_baseline_selection: Highest exact expected verified completion, then sampled completion, then lowest sampled total cost; ties broken by name
protocol.promotion: All gates must pass. No allowed regression tolerance. Failure retains existing defaults.
protocol.timing: Tokens and action latency are declared estimates for belief tasks. Decision latency is measured. Weighted cost = tokens + .01*(declared action ms + measured decision ms). No real tool time is claimed for belief simulation.
protocol.provenance: Fresh instances after freeze; generator families and fixture templates are developer-known. This is not an unseen-repository or natural-language benchmark.

limitations: Numeric declared-world decisions, known generator families and controlled supplied-patch fixtures. Fresh seeds are reserved from training but not proof of general real-world competence. Goal/permission masks are supplied rules. A single shared-Mac timing session is not a precision performance benchmark.
